FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A01
Never swerve into traffic or off the road for an animal, since the evasion crash beats the animal strike [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A01
Animal odds fall with dawn-and-dusk care, heed of crossing signs, woods, and water, roadside scans for eye shine, and October-through-December deer watch [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A01
Near animals slow down, flash others, ease off with taps and horn, mind freezing deer, and brake hard when the rear is clear [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A01
Unavoidable strikes hold the lane under control, and large-animal crashes go to law enforcement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A01
Smoke, fog, and downpours demand real headlights on low beams, lights with wipers, defrosted glass, and painted-line guides [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A02
Murky driving also kills cabin distractions, watches for crawling and parked rigs, and keeps glass and lamps clean [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A02
Wipers summon headlights, fresh rains slick oiled pavement into longer stops, and gaps grow accordingly [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A02
Hydroplaning floats tires off the road into skids, worsened by soft pressure, bald tread, and speed [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A02
Soaked brakes pull or fade until gently dried, and flooded roads always turn back since depth and current hide [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A02
High beams reveal 450 feet and suit speeds past 25 MPH, while oncoming glare shrinks night sight [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A03
Night law lights sunset to sunrise, dims within 500 feet of oncoming and 300 ahead, bans parking-lights-only driving, and parks lit outside towns [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A03
Night craft avoids overdriving lamps, rests eyes off bright zones, skims lane lines past staring, and hugs right for one-eyed traffic [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0081]
